name: Thread Generator
description: Cut a 3D-printable thread into a shaft or hole. Select its round face in the design, then Run. Hover a field for what it does. The thread is an editable feature in the timeline; one Ctrl+Z takes the whole run back.

size.title: Size
size.description:
Which thread to cut: diameter x pitch, like M8x1 (8 mm across, 1 mm from crest to crest).
Auto reads the selected face. A shaft gets its own diameter (Ø8 → M8). So does a hole of a whole millimetre (Ø14 → M14), so a shaft and a hole drawn the same size fit each other. Any other hole counts as a tap drill, one pitch smaller than the thread (Ø6.8 → M8).
Or type a size: M8x1, M10 (the pitch then comes from Pitch) or a UNC size like 1/4-20.

pitch.title: Pitch
pitch.description:
Distance from one thread crest to the next. A larger pitch gives deeper, coarser teeth: they print more reliably and screw in with fewer turns, but there are fewer of them over the same length.
1 mm: fine threads, from M4; needs a printer that holds small detail. 1.25-1.75 mm: in between, a good choice when 1 mm is too fine and 2 mm too coarse. 2 or 2.5 mm: print well at 0.2-0.3 mm layers. 3.5 or 5 mm: big, sturdy parts, from M8.
ISO standard uses the metric coarse pitch (M8: 1.25 mm), so metal screws and nuts fit.
Ignored when Size names a pitch (M8x1).

tolerance.title: Tolerance
tolerance.description:
The play between the parts. This part is made looser by this much on its diameter: O.2 makes a shaft 0.2 mm thinner or a hole 0.2 mm wider. Printing both the bolt and the nut? Each gets its own tolerance, so the play adds up.
Start with O.2 on both. A bit tight: O.25 or O.3. Hard to screw in: O.35 or O.4. Wobbly: O.15 or O.1. O.0 is the exact size, with no play. O.8 is very loose.

height.title: Height
height.description:
How far the teeth stick out, as a share of a full ISO tooth (at a 1 mm pitch, 100% is about 0.54 mm and 85% about 0.46 mm).
Lower cuts the sharp tips of the teeth flat. Flat tips print cleaner and are less likely to bind, but the teeth grip less deep, so the thread holds less. The flanks stay where they are, so the play (Tolerance) doesn't change.
85% suits most printers. 90-100% for the strongest thread; 70-80% for a coarse nozzle, or if the thread binds. Use the same height on the bolt and the nut.

length.title: Length
length.description:
How much of the face to thread, along its axis. Empty threads the whole face.
A shorter thread starts at the face's free end (on a face open at both ends, the end nearest where you clicked it), and leaves the rest smooth: a plain shank under a bolt head, say.
